mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (0.0 → 19.0) signals normalization of essential shopping patterns. This confidence in routine errands spills over into discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within the same weekly cycles, driving net positive RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 19 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 10 points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely depressed (-34.9 at t-0w) while RETAIL_REC has recovered to -26.9. This divergence indicates outdoor recreation constraints are binding, forcing substitution toward indoor retail venues. Continued PARKS suppression will sustain this substitution effect, elevating RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -34.9 vs RETAIL_REC at -26.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -20 within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines below -30 in week t+1 despite PARKS remaining suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined monotonically from 19.1 to 13.7 over four weeks, indicating accelerating out-of-home activity resumption. This behavioral shift toward external mobility will compound over the next two weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher as the population spends less time at home.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 5.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior two-week mean within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -22.3 after declining from -29.0, signaling plateau in office return. This stalled workplace recovery will constrain weekday retail footfall from commuter populations, preventing RETAIL_REC from rising significantly over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change by less than 2 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -22.3 with minimal week-on-week change
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC exceeds its four-week mean by more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -35.0 to -20.1 over four weeks, indicating relaxation of mobility restrictions. If TRANSIT continues this recovery trajectory and crosses -15 within the next week, public transportation capacity will enable retail cluster visits, accelerating RETAIL_REC growth over the subsequent three weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -15 in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 14.9 points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not exceed -15 by week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines despite TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM (+19.0) and RETAIL_REC (-26.9) trajectories indicates behavioral reorientation toward mixed-purpose trips. As consumers rebuild confidence in out-of-home activity through essential shopping, they will incrementally add discretionary retail stops. This bundling effect will lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 15 and RETAIL_REC rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below 15 in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise by at least 2 points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: All mobility categories except RESIDENTIAL show consistent week-on-week improvement over the four-week window, indicating a seasonal or cyclical recovery pattern independent of specific policy triggers. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher as the recovery cycle continues.
failure_condition: Any of RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, or PARKS declines in week t+1 relative to week t-0w, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC recovery has decelerated from -40.7 to -26.9 (improvement rate declining from 4.4 to 4.1 points per week). If this deceleration continues, RETAIL_REC will approach a saturation point where further gains become marginal, resulting in net negative direction over the next four weeks as the recovery exhausts available demand.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week improvement falls below 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improvement rate declined from 4.4 to 4.1 points per week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 4 points in week t+1, or mean RETAIL_REC over next 28 days exceeds mean over last 28 days.
